text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Severity: P1 - KV cache memory growth + NCCL stalls on tp-cluster-7. Alert threshold: GPU mem > 90% & NCCL stalls > 5m. Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1723459999
Maya R: I'm on it. seeing a large spike in kv_cache_entries per-shard starting ~1723459500. paging metrics show spike in page-in ops.
Oli K: oncall-eng here, paging notice received. Any customer-facing errors yet?
Samir: We have increased 5xxs for generation API for some hosted tenants, ~15% errors for 12 minutes in eu-west. Dedicated customers reported timeouts. No data loss.
Jin Park: initial hypothesis: continuous-batching change rolled an hour ago to increase max_batch_size from 32 -> 64 which replicated across tp shards and caused uneven KV partition sizes. Some ranks got hot and hit eviction thrash -> page thrash -> NCCL stalls during allreduce.
Maya R: rolling back continuous-batch config now. Patch: 
```
# runtime config change
continuous_batching.enabled: false
continuous_batching.max_batch_size: 32
```
Applying to cluster tp-cluster-7 via deploy manager.
oncall-eng: Please coordinate hotfix steps, we may need a shard rebalance and rolling restart.
Oli K: Agreed. Plan: (1) disable continuous batching, (2) reduce batch target to 16 for headroom, (3) force KV shard rebalance to uniform partitioning, (4) drain & restart affected GPU pods (one-at-a-time), (5) monitor NCCL stall metric and customer error rate.
Samir: I'll run the rebalance tool. Command: 
```
./tools/kv_rebalance --cluster tp-cluster-7 --mode uniform --dry-run=false --max-inflight=1
```
Starting now. ETA ~5-8 min to finish metadata move.
Maya R: Pushing config rollback via orchestrator: commit 9f3b2a4 -> rolling apply.
incident-bot: Deploy started by Maya R (commit 9f3b2a4). Progress: 1/12 nodes updated.
Jin Park: Observing drop in per-shard hot-key ratio after rebalance step ~1723460500. NCCL stalls decreased from 7m to 30s on average.
Oli K: We're seeing 503s drop to baseline but latency still elevated. Any long-tail page-ins?
Samir: Page-in rate trending down; KV memory pressure reduced but one rank still higher than others. I'll throttle its accept queue and evict less aggressively for now. Hotfix needed: fix shard assignment hash that biased rank indices when batch_size > 32.
Maya R: Can you capture the stack trace/trace logs for the stalled rank? Paste here.
Samir: logs (truncated): 
```
2024-09-11T12:12:04Z tp-rank-3 worker: kv_shard_size=1.8GB, kv_hit_rate=0.12
2024-09-11T12:12:05Z tp-rank-3 nccl: allreduce stalled (timeout after 60000ms)
2024-09-11T12:12:05Z tp-rank-3 runtime: batch_size=64 target_seq=1024
```
Oli K: That matches the hypothesis. Hotfix strategy: patch shard hashing to include tensor-parallel rank salt and limit bucket sizing when max_batch_size > 32. We'll do a hotpatch and then restart the single bad rank to avoid full cluster restart.
Jin Park: I'll prepare the patch. Diff (conceptual): 
```
- bucket = hash(key) % num_shards
+ bucket = (hash(key) ^ tp_rank_salt) % num_shards
+ if max_batch_size > 32: bucket = bucket % (num_shards / min(4, tp_size))
```
Applying to runtime repo, branch: fix/kv-shard-salt-1723459999, PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4821
Maya R: After rebalance and config rollback, customer error alerts are reduced. Notifying support to update impacted tenant list.
incident-bot: Support ticket created: #INC-7842 (impacted-hosted-tenants).
Samir: Hotpatch deployed to tp-rank-3 (restart). Post-restart status: NCCL stalls dropped to 0 over 10m window. KV shard sizes roughly even within 5%.
Oli K: Can we confirm SLA impact window and affected customers? Samir or Maya please confirm numbers.
Maya R: Looking at request logs: elevated 5xxs from 1723459400 -> 1723461200 (30 minutes). Approx 3.2% of total gen requests for eu-west and a handful of dedicated endpoints had timeouts. Support will notify customers; no persisted customer data affected.
Jin Park: Root cause summary: combination of continuous-batching increase + shard hashing bias produced heavy hotspots on a subset of TP ranks causing memory thrash and NCCL stalls during collective ops. The high aggregation batch size amplified imbalance.
Maya R: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem owner: Jin Park. Action items assigned: 
- Jin Park: fix/complete shard hashing patch + unit tests (ETA 48h)
- Samir: add automated rebalance alert when per-shard variance > 30% (ETA 24h)
- Mali/Support: customer comms + variables for SLA credits (ETA 4h)
- Ops: add canary rule preventing cluster-wide batch_size bumps without staged rollout (ETA 72h)
oncall-eng: Thanks folks. Any outstanding risks?
Maya R: We'll keep an eye on tp-cluster-7 for next 4 hours. I'll keep thread updated.
incident-bot: Incident downgraded to P2 at 1723462800.
Oli K: marking as resolved once postmortem drafted. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Maya R: Closing thread notes: no customer data exposure, root cause linked to runtime sharding + config rollout. Postmortem will include timeline + CI checks.
